title: Stationary hourly models with identical two-hour laws gave daily flood risks of 65.01% and 86.56% at 5% hourly risk
abstract: We test whether full two-hour distributions determine daily flood risk when hourly processes are stationary and mixing. Two explicit processes have standard normal hourly values and independent normal pairs at every lag. At a constant threshold with 5% hourly exceedance probability, their 24-hour risks are 65.0067% and 86.5629%. Finite rational sums prove both values. Any method that uses only the common hour and pair laws must have an absolute error of at least 10.7781 percentage points in one process. Independent regeneration blocks of length 23 or 24 make both processes stationary and mixing. A common normal factor gives equal positive pair dependence in a second test. At within-block correlation 0.5 and 5% hourly risk, two daily risks are 43.3056% and 47.1050%. We provide count-law optimization, exact arithmetic and independent hourly simulation. This extends prior correlation-only flood tests by fixing full pair laws and removing their non-ergodic extension. The general probability facts are established prior work. These are synthetic flat-tide tests, not a fit to coastal data or an estimate of NOAA forecast bias. Full-pair validation alone cannot validate a daily extreme forecast.

display.caption: Equal full pair laws do not identify daily risk, even in stationary mixing processes. The left panel is exact. The right panel uses one-dimensional integration and count optimization.
